questions.stem: Why do hydrophytes often have stomata on the upper surface of their floating leaves rather than the lower surface?

options.text: Because the upper surface receives more light for photosynthesis
Because the lower surface is in contact with water, which would block the stomata
Because wind only blows across the upper surface
Because carbon dioxide is only available above the leaf

questions.explanation: In hydrophytes with floating leaves (such as water lilies), the lower leaf surface is in contact with the water. If stomata were on the lower surface, they would be submerged and unable to exchange gases with the air. Having stomata on the upper surface, which is exposed to the air, allows gas exchange to occur.
